Title: A priceless gift
NewsSubTitle: AKU honours the spirit of volunteerism
NewsSummary: On Tuesday November 25, the Aga Khan University family gathered to honour 87 of its current volunteers while paying tribute to those who have so admirably served since the inception of the volunteer programme in 1987.

content.text: There are those in this world who give of their time and effort, indeed give of themselves selflessly with no regard for any compensation, a casual thank you here and there being more than enough for them. Working without any official designation or authority, yet helping everyone, being there when it matters, they are volunteers.

On Tuesday November 25, the Aga Khan University family gathered to honour 87 of its current volunteers while paying tribute to those who have so admirably served since the inception of the volunteer programme in 1987. Of the 87 volunteers receiving special mention, 27 have served for 5,000 hours, 14 have given 10,000 hours of their time and one volunteer who has given an awe-inspiring 20,000 hours of service to the University.

In his welcome address, President Firoz Rasul acknowledged that the life of a volunteer was one filled with challenge, "You show kindness, stay calm and diligently perform your duties no matter the circumstances you face - and they are not always easy, as people are not always at their best."

Included in the 87 were 43 Time Knowledge Nazrana volunteers who have completed their service at AKU as well as 2 overseas volunteers currently at the University. Since the inception of the TKN programme 96 overseas and 69 local TKN volunteers have contributed their expertise in fields ranging from nursing to architecture, information technology to supply chain management, English language instruction to microbiology to mention a few.
He reaffirmed the University's commitment to its volunteers siting the fact that 340 of the current staff were at one time volunteers.

As the University moves forward, the importance of volunteers will remain as strong as ever as echoed in the words of the Chancellor, His Highness the Aga Khan, "In whatever we do, at whatever level, we have always been reliant upon volunteers ... especially in today's difficult circumstances, we must never lose sight of nor undervalue the secret of our Aga Khan Network's success, the element which underpins its professionalism. The heart and lifeblood of our network [are] the voluntary workers; the Boards, the Committees, the volunteers - young and old - who contribute their time and efforts."
